tier_justification: Reference point: reflexivity of contextual approximation is immediate from its definition (contextual equivalence originates with J. H. Morris Jr. 1968).
plain_claim: Every module contextually refines itself (`CtxRefines M M`); this is a reference point, immediate from the definition.
depth_justification: The identity map on `HasBehavior entry (link C M) fuel arg out`.
nonvacuity_witness: The open module `openCallerMod` (`0` calls the import `1`) contextually refines itself.
non_claims: `CtxRefines`/`EntryRefines` compare outcome sets at the same call-depth fuel, and `outOfFuel` is one of the compared outcomes. They therefore do constrain divergence: a target that may fail to terminate where the source terminates does not refine it (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_rejects_new_divergence`). They imply inclusion of may-divergence in the sense of `MayDiverge` (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_reflects_mayDiverge`; with binary `choose`, `MayDiverge` coincides with the existence of an infinite call chain, an equivalence not formalized here), and they are strictly finer than inclusion of eventual results or of divergence-sensitive behaviour because they also fix call depth (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_fixes_call_depth`). 'Divergence is not observed' applies only to the partial-correctness results.

Every function a module defines is exported and can be called by a context, and `CtxRefines M M'` implies `SameDom M M'` (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_sameDom`). So contextual refinement here forbids adding, removing or renaming any function, including compiler-introduced helpers (clones, outlined code) and dead internal helpers. The model has no private or static symbols, so it says nothing about transformations of non-exported code.
Does not make `CtxRefines` symmetric: `choose01Mod ⊑ const0Mod` holds while the converse fails (`Toy.Link.Examples.cex_ctxRefines_not_symm`).

Toy model: stateless first-order functions of one unbounded integer argument, modules as finite association lists, no memory and no concurrency; says nothing directly about C, Rust, or assembly linking.
prior_art: James Hiram Morris Jr., 'Lambda-calculus models of programming languages', PhD thesis, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT Project MAC report MAC-TR-57, 1968; the MIT DSpace record, hdl:1721.1/64850, dates the degree 1969): origin of contextual (observational) equivalence. The thesis record and secondary accounts were checked; the page of the definition was not.
design_question: Which per-module guarantees compose into whole-program guarantees under linking, which apparently natural per-module notions do not, and what extra structure (fuel or a well-founded measure, spec refinement, interface-only assumptions) is genuinely needed? (Reference point.)

tier_justification: Transitivity of contextual approximation; the only non-immediate step is that `Linkable C M₂` follows from `Linkable C M₁` because `CtxRefines` forces equal domains (`ctxRefines_sameDom`).
plain_claim: If `CtxRefines M₁ M₂` and `CtxRefines M₂ M₃`, then `CtxRefines M₁ M₃`, with no extra domain or linkability hypothesis on the middle module `M₂`.

hypotheses.name: CtxRefines M₁ M₂
hypotheses.purpose: first refinement step; also gives `SameDom M₁ M₂`, so every context disjoint from `M₁` is disjoint from `M₂`. Tightness is immediate for any relation that is not total (the counterexample takes `M₂ = M₃`).

hypotheses.name: CtxRefines M₂ M₃
hypotheses.purpose: second refinement step

depth_justification: Derives `Linkable C M₂` via `ctxRefines_sameDom`, then chains the two outcome inclusions.
non_claims: `CtxRefines` compares outcome sets at the same call-depth fuel, including `outOfFuel`; it constrains divergence and fixes call depth (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_rejects_new_divergence`, `Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_fixes_call_depth`). Adding or removing a call can break `CtxRefines` even when results agree at every fuel of at least `2`: `Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_fixes_call_depth` gives such a pair, in both directions.
Every defined function is exported; `CtxRefines` forces equal domains (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_sameDom`). The model has no private symbols.

Unlike Patterson and Ahmed's discussion of vertical compositionality (which they distinguish from transitivity), this result relates modules of one language only; it says nothing about multi-pass compilers between different languages.
prior_art: Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, 'The next 700 compiler correctness theorems (functional pearl)', PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 29 pp., 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§5.4, p. 85:18, 'Digression: Vertical Compositionality vs. Transitivity').

Youngju Song, Minki Cho, Dongjoo Kim, Yonghyun Kim, Jeehoon Kang, and Chung-Kil Hur, 'CompCertM: CompCert with C-assembly linking and lightweight modular verification', PACMPL 4(POPL), Article 23, 31 pp., 2020, doi:10.1145/3371091 (§2.3, Theorem 2.1, `VerComp`: vertical composition of refinement).

Jérémie Koenig and Zhong Shao, 'CompCertO: compiling certified open C components', PLDI '21, pp. 1095-1109, 2021, doi:10.1145/3453483.3454097 (§3.3, Theorem 3.7: open forward simulations compose vertically).
design_question: Which per-module guarantees compose into whole-program guarantees under linking, which apparently natural per-module notions do not, and what extra structure (fuel or a well-founded measure, spec refinement, interface-only assumptions) is genuinely needed?

tier_justification: Contextual approximation is a precongruence by construction: a context for `link M₁ M₂` is re-associated as a context for each component.
plain_claim: If `CtxRefines M₁ M₁'`, `CtxRefines M₂ M₂'`, and `Linkable M₁ M₂`, then `CtxRefines (link M₁ M₂) (link M₁' M₂')`; `Linkable M₁' M₂'` is derived, not assumed.

hypotheses.name: CtxRefines M₁ M₁'
hypotheses.purpose: contextual refinement of the left module (also gives `SameDom M₁ M₁'`)

hypotheses.name: CtxRefines M₂ M₂'
hypotheses.purpose: contextual refinement of the right module (also gives `SameDom M₂ M₂'`)

hypotheses.name: Linkable M₁ M₂
hypotheses.purpose: disjointness: without it, `M₁` can shadow a name that `M₂` uses internally (symbol interposition), and `CtxRefines M₂ M₂'` only quantifies over disjoint contexts

depth_justification: Re-associates and commutes the disjoint contexts `link C M₂'` and `link C M₁` (`lookup_link_assoc`, `lookup_link_comm`) and applies each hypothesis once.
nonvacuity_witness: Caller `[(0, call 1 var)]` linked with `[(1, choose (lit 0) (lit 1))]`, refined to the same caller linked with `[(1, lit 0)]`.
non_claims: Precongruence is close to definitional here: contexts are stateless first-order modules and compose by linking. Unlike CompCertO Theorem 3.4 and CompCertM HorComp (which needs self-related modules), it says nothing about simulation-based compiler correctness, where horizontal composition is a substantive theorem about memory and rely/guarantee conventions.
Does not hold for non-disjoint (shadowing) linking (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_link_congr_without_linkable`).

`CtxRefines` constrains divergence and fixes call depth (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_fixes_call_depth`); a per-module pass that adds or removes a call need not be a contextual refinement (the same counterexample gives one that is not, in each direction), so this theorem does not cover such a pass unless `CtxRefines` is proved for it. Specification-based separate compilation (`separate-compilation-preserves-verifiability`) admits such passes but gives no behavioural relation.
Every defined function is exported; `CtxRefines` forces equal domains. The model has no private symbols.
prior_art: Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, 'The next 700 compiler correctness theorems (functional pearl)', PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 29 pp., 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§5.2, p. 85:14, 'Digression: Horizontal Compositionality vs. Source-Independent Linking').
Youngju Song et al., 'CompCertM', PACMPL 4(POPL), Article 23, 2020, doi:10.1145/3371091 (§2.3, Theorem 2.1, `HorComp`, stated for self-related modules).
Jérémie Koenig and Zhong Shao, 'CompCertO', PLDI '21, pp. 1095-1109, 2021, doi:10.1145/3453483.3454097 (§3.3, Theorem 3.4: horizontal composition of simulations).
design_question: Which per-module guarantees compose into whole-program guarantees under linking, which apparently natural per-module notions do not, and what extra structure (fuel or a well-founded measure, spec refinement, interface-only assumptions) is genuinely needed?

tier_justification: Folklore (contextual equivalence presupposes a common interface) made precise: here equal domains are derived, because a call to an undefined name is observable as `undefinedCall` even with the empty context.
plain_claim: If `CtxRefines M M'`, then `M` and `M'` define exactly the same function names (`SameDom M M'`); hence adding, deleting, or renaming any function breaks contextual refinement in this model.

hypotheses.name: CtxRefines M M'
hypotheses.purpose: the empty context at fuel `1` distinguishes a defined from an undefined name

depth_justification: Probe each name with the empty context at fuel `1` (`eval_one_undefinedCall_iff`).
non_claims: Depends on two modelling choices: `undefinedCall` is an ordinary observable outcome, and contexts need not close the program (the entry may be any name, including one neither module defines). Linking never fails: unresolved references are allowed and fail only at run time, so deleting an exported function is modelled as a change of run-time behaviour, whereas in real toolchains it is typically a link-time error. A source `undefinedCall` does not license arbitrary target behaviour (contrast Leroy 2009, §2.1).
The model has no private or static symbols: every definition is an export. The result says nothing about adding or removing non-exported helpers in a language with symbol hiding.
Does not say that equal domains suffice for contextual refinement.
prior_art: Xavier Leroy, 'Formal verification of a realistic compiler', Communications of the ACM 52(7):107-115, 2009, doi:10.1145/1538788.1538814 (§2.1: whole-program semantic preservation; going-wrong source behaviours relax preservation, unlike here).
design_question: Which apparently natural per-module transformations (deleting unused exports, introducing helpers) fail contextual refinement, and why?

tier_justification: Instances of `ctxRefines_sameDom`; no source states these particular transformations, so labelled folklore made precise.
plain_claim: For example, deleting an exported function that no in-module code calls (`deadSrc` → `deadTgt`, both closed) or adding an unused helper function (`[(0, lit 0)]` → `[(0, lit 0), (7, lit 0)]`) preserves refinement (both directions) at the designated entry `0`, yet fails `CtxRefines` because the domain changes. The failure half is general: every transformation that changes the set of defined function names fails `CtxRefines` (`ctxRefines_sameDom`, card `ctx-refines-forces-same-domain`); this is domain observability, not a context-interaction phenomenon.
depth_justification: Entry-0 refinement by fuel case split; `¬ SameDom` by `decide`; `¬ CtxRefines` from `ctxRefines_sameDom`.
nonvacuity_witness: `deadSrc = [(0, lit 42), (1, lit 7)]` vs `deadTgt = [(0, lit 42)]`; `[(0, lit 0)]` vs `[(0, lit 0), (7, lit 0)]`.
non_claims: This is an immediate consequence of `ctxRefines_sameDom`; calling the deleted function with the empty context already separates the pair. It does not exhibit callbacks, shared memory, or pointer leakage.

The model has no private symbols. In a language where the helper or the deleted function is static (not exported), these transformations may well be contextual refinements; nothing here speaks to that.
`undefinedCall` is observable and linking never fails; in real toolchains deleting a referenced export is typically a link-time error.
prior_art: Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, 'The next 700 compiler correctness theorems (functional pearl)', PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§2, p. 85:3: the whole-program theorem 'says absolutely nothing about what (if anything) the compiler does for partial programs').
design_question: Which apparently natural per-module transformations fail contextual refinement, and is the failure due to contexts or merely to the interface?

tier_justification: Folklore that contexts matter only through the interactions they can have with a module, made precise for stateless first-order modules; no source states this exact equivalence.
plain_claim: If the source module or the target module is closed (`ClosedModule M ∨ ClosedModule M'`), then contextual refinement coincides with standalone refinement at every entry point (`CtxRefines M M' ↔ StandaloneRefines M M'`); contexts can only matter when both modules are open.

hypotheses.name: ClosedModule M ∨ ClosedModule M'
hypotheses.purpose: if the target is closed, a disjoint context neither changes the target's own functions nor removes any outcome of the source other than `undefinedCall`; if the source is closed, standalone refinement forces the target never to reach an unresolved name from a defined entry, so the context cannot affect it. Either disjunct alone suffices.

depth_justification: Induction on fuel over the context's entries, using `eval_link_closed`, `eval_link_right_of_no_undefinedCall`, `closedModule_no_undefinedCall` and the monotonicity lemma `eval_link_superset_non_undefinedCall`.
nonvacuity_witness: Open source `[(0, choose (lit 1) (call 5 var))]` and closed target `const1Mod`: standalone refinement holds, so the theorem yields `CtxRefines` (removing a branch that calls an import). Closed-source disjunct: closed source `const1Mod = [(0, lit 1)]` and syntactically open target `deadImportTgt = [(0, ifLe (lit 1) (lit 0) (call 5 var) (lit 1))]` (the external call is dead): standalone refinement holds, and so `CtxRefines` holds.
non_claims: For closed modules the only gap between refinement at a designated entry and contextual refinement is the other exported entries (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_closed_main_entry_refines_not_ctxRefines`); no context is needed to exhibit it.

Relies on the absence of state, memory, and pointers: contexts can interact with a module only through calls and return values. In languages with shared state or address-taking, closed modules can still be distinguished by contexts.
`CtxRefines` compares outcomes in lockstep call depth and every definition is exported (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_sameDom`); so does `StandaloneRefines` (by `sameDom_of_standaloneRefines`).
With both modules open the equivalence fails (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_collapse_without_closed_side`).
prior_art: Gordon Stewart, Lennart Beringer, Santiago Cuellar, and Andrew W. Appel, 'Compositional CompCert', POPL '15, pp. 275-287, 2015, doi:10.1145/2676726.2676985 (§1: CompCert's original correctness statement is limited to whole programs; §3, Definition 1: contextual equivalence as equitermination under all contexts).
Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, 'The next 700 compiler correctness theorems (functional pearl)', PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§2, p. 85:3).
design_question: When does a whole-program (closed) refinement check suffice for contextual refinement, and when is genuine context quantification needed?

tier_justification: Folklore that whole-program refinement at `main` says nothing about other exported entries, made precise; the cited sources state the general gap, not this transformation.
plain_claim: Specializing an exported function `1` of a closed module to the argument `5` used by its only in-module caller preserves refinement in both directions at the designated entry `0` (with equal domains), but already fails refinement at entry `1` with no context, so it is not a contextual refinement.
depth_justification: Fuel case split for entry `0`; `decide` at entry `1`, fuel `1`; `¬ CtxRefines` via `standaloneRefines_of_ctxRefines`.
nonvacuity_witness: `specSrc = [(0, call 1 (lit 5)), (1, var)]`, `specTgt = [(0, call 1 (lit 5)), (1, lit 5)]`; entry `1` on argument `9` returns `9` vs `5`.
non_claims: For closed modules, contextual refinement in this model coincides with standalone refinement at every entry point (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_iff_standaloneRefines_of_closed_source_or_target`). This counterexample is already witnessed by calling function `1` directly with the empty context. It shows only that refinement at one designated entry does not imply refinement at all exported entries. It does not exhibit any context-interaction phenomenon such as callbacks, shared memory or pointer leakage; for a counterexample in which the context supplies behaviour, see `cex-open-specialization-standalone-refinement-not-contextual`.
Every definition is exported; specialization via a fresh private clone cannot be expressed (a clone is a new export and fails `CtxRefines` by `Toy.Link.ctxRefines_sameDom`).
Does not claim that every optimization of an exported body fails: an in-place `x + 0 ↦ x` rewrite is a contextual refinement (`Toy.Link.Examples.positive_control_in_place_export_optimization`).
prior_art: F. Lockwood Morris, 'Advice on structuring compilers and proving them correct', POPL '73, pp. 144-152, 1973, doi:10.1145/512927.512941 (whole-program semantics-preservation diagram, as summarized by Patterson and Ahmed 2019, §2, pp. 85:3-85:4; primary text not checked).
Xavier Leroy, 'Formal verification of a realistic compiler', CACM 52(7):107-115, 2009, doi:10.1145/1538788.1538814 (§2.1: semantic preservation for whole programs).
Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§2, p. 85:3).
design_question: Which per-module guarantees compose into whole-program guarantees under linking, and which apparently natural per-module notions do not?

tier_justification: Folklore (refinement checked in one program, or with imports unresolved, does not survive other linking contexts) made precise with an open module whose import is supplied by the context.
plain_claim: For open modules `openSpecSrc = [(0, call 1 (lit 3)), (1, call 5 var)]` and its specialization `openSpecTgt` (`1` forwards the constant `3` used by its only in-module caller to the import `5`), refinement holds in both directions at every entry when the modules run standalone, and at the designated entry `0` of the program `link identityImport _` they ship in; yet in that program calling `1(9)` separates them, a context whose import `5` calls back into `1` separates them even at entry `0`, and `CtxRefines` fails.
depth_justification: Equal evaluation lists by fuel case analysis; separating behaviours by `decide` at fuel `2` (entry `1`) and fuel `5` (callback context, entry `0`).
nonvacuity_witness: Identity import `[(5, var)]`: entry `1` on `9` returns `9` vs `3`. Callback import `[(5, ifLe var (lit 3) (call 1 (lit 9)) var)]`: entry `0` at fuel `5` returns `9` vs out of fuel (the specialized module loops through the callback).
non_claims: Both modules are open, and this is necessary: if either were closed, standalone refinement would imply `CtxRefines` (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_iff_standaloneRefines_of_closed_source_or_target`).

Does not show that refinement at entry `0` fails under every context: in the shipped program it holds. It shows that neither standalone refinement at all entries nor refinement at the designated entry of one particular program implies contextual refinement.
The interaction is first-order (calls and return values, including callbacks); there is no shared memory or pointer leakage in the model.
`CtxRefines` constrains divergence: the callback separation at entry `0` is a newly introduced divergence.
prior_art: Gordon Stewart, Lennart Beringer, Santiago Cuellar, and Andrew W. Appel, 'Compositional CompCert', POPL '15, pp. 275-287, 2015, doi:10.1145/2676726.2676985 (§1; §3, Definition 1).
Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§2, p. 85:3).
design_question: Which per-module guarantees compose into whole-program guarantees under linking, which apparently natural per-module notions do not, and when is quantification over contexts genuinely needed?

tier_justification: Folklore (fuel-indexed refinement observes non-termination) made precise for this definition.
plain_claim: If `CtxRefines M M'` and the context `C` is disjoint from `M`, then whenever `link C M'` may diverge at an entry and argument (`outOfFuel` at every fuel), so may `link C M`.

hypotheses.name: CtxRefines M M'
hypotheses.purpose: outcomes, including `outOfFuel`, are compared at every fuel

hypotheses.name: Linkable C M
hypotheses.purpose: `CtxRefines` quantifies only over disjoint contexts; an overlapping context can shadow a name that one module uses. (`Linkable C M'` is derived from it via `ctxRefines_sameDom`.)

depth_justification: Instantiate `CtxRefines` with the outcome `outOfFuel` at each fuel.
nonvacuity_witness: `chooseLoopMod = [(0, choose (call 0 var) (lit 0))]` ⊑ `selfLoopMod = [(0, call 0 var)]` with the empty context; the target may diverge.
non_claims: `MayDiverge` is 'out of fuel at every fuel'. That this coincides with an infinite execution relies on finite (binary) branching and is not formalized here.
Does not say `CtxRefines` is a divergence-sensitive refinement in the usual sense: it is strictly finer, because it also fixes call depth (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_fixes_call_depth`).
Partial-correctness notions (`FnPartialCorrect`, `ProgramPartialCorrect`) accept `outOfFuel` and therefore do not observe divergence; this theorem is about the refinement relations only.
prior_art: Tobias Nipkow, 'Hoare logics for recursive procedures and unbounded nondeterminism', CSL 2002, LNCS 2471, pp. 103-119, Springer, 2002, doi:10.1007/3-540-45793-3_8 (§2: semantics indexed by 'at most n nested procedure invocations', the same call-depth index as the fuel here).
design_question: What exactly does fuel-indexed contextual refinement observe about non-termination and call structure?

tier_justification: Folklore consequence of lockstep fuel indexing, made precise.
plain_claim: `directMod = [(0, lit 0), (1, lit 0)]` and `viaCallMod = [(0, call 1 var), (1, lit 0)]` have equal domains and evaluate identically at every entry and argument once fuel is at least `2`, yet neither contextually refines the other: here adding or removing the call changes the call depth on the path from entry `0`, which `CtxRefines` observes because it compares outcomes at equal fuel. Whether every added or removed call breaks `CtxRefines` is not proved here.
depth_justification: Evaluation at fuel `n + 2` by `simp`; separations at fuel `1` by `decide`.
nonvacuity_witness: At fuel `1`, `viaCallMod` is out of fuel at entry `0` and `directMod` returns `0`.
non_claims: Shows that `CtxRefines` is strictly finer than inclusion of eventual results; it does not claim that real compilers must preserve call depth. A refinement relation insensitive to call depth (e.g. comparing outcomes for some sufficiently large fuel) is a different design not studied here.
Passes that keep the call structure, such as constant folding of `x + 0`, are contextual refinements (`Toy.Link.Examples.passCtxRefines_pos`).
prior_art: Tobias Nipkow, CSL 2002, LNCS 2471, pp. 103-119, doi:10.1007/3-540-45793-3_8 (§2: call-depth-indexed semantics).
design_question: What exactly does fuel-indexed contextual refinement observe, and which optimizations does it therefore exclude?

tier_justification: The rule of recursive invocation for partial correctness (Hoare 1971), proved sound by induction on call depth as in Nipkow 2002 §§2-3; mechanized in Isabelle/HOL by Nipkow and in Schirmer's Simpl.
plain_claim: If every function with a satisfiable precondition is defined in `P` (`SpecsImplemented P S`) and every body satisfies its contract assuming all callees satisfy theirs (`ModuleVerifiedPartial P S S`), then `P` is partially correct for `S`, with no termination measure.

hypotheses.name: SpecsImplemented P S
hypotheses.purpose: rules out `undefinedCall` at calls permitted by `S`

hypotheses.name: ModuleVerifiedPartial P S S
hypotheses.purpose: each body establishes its postcondition under `wpPartial S`, assuming callees satisfy `S`

depth_justification: Induction on fuel lifting the already proved one-frame soundness lemma `wpPartial_sound_evalExprWith`; about fifteen lines.
nonvacuity_witness: Mutually recursive `even`/`odd` program `evenOddProg` with parity contract `evenOddSpec`. Applying the theorem yields `ProgramPartialCorrect evenOddProg evenOddSpec` (`Toy.Link.Examples.evenOddProg_partial_correct`).
non_claims: Partial correctness only: `outOfFuel` is always accepted, so divergence is not observed; a diverging loop is partially correct for any postcondition (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ag_total_unsound_without_measure`).
Contracts are on a single integer argument and result; no state, frames, auxiliary variables or adaptation rules are modelled; integers are unbounded.
Each call is assumed independently via `(S fn).post`, so cross-call facts (e.g. `f(x) - f(x) = 0`) are not available unless the postcondition determines the result.
prior_art: C. A. R. Hoare, 'Procedures and parameters: An axiomatic approach', Symposium on Semantics of Algorithmic Languages, LNM 188, pp. 102-116, Springer, 1971, doi:10.1007/BFb0059696 (rule of recursive invocation; the page of the rule was not checked).

Tobias Nipkow, 'Hoare logics for recursive procedures and unbounded nondeterminism', CSL 2002, LNCS 2471, pp. 103-119, Springer, 2002, doi:10.1007/3-540-45793-3_8 (§2: semantics with 'at most n nested procedure invocations'; §3: soundness of partial correctness proved by induction on the call depth; mechanized in Isabelle/HOL; checked against the author's preprint, whose pagination differs from the LNCS pages).

Norbert Schirmer, 'A Sequential Imperative Programming Language: Syntax, Semantics, Hoare Logics and Verification Environment', Archive of Formal Proofs, 2008 (Simpl: sound and complete Hoare logics for partial and total correctness with mutually recursive procedures, in Isabelle/HOL).

Martín Abadi and Leslie Lamport, 'Conjoining specifications', ACM TOPLAS 17(3):507-535, 1995, doi:10.1145/203095.201069 (analogy only: circular assume-guarantee composition is sound for safety, where the guarantee must hold one step longer than the assumption (§2.2, p. 513; §5.2, p. 529); here the fuel decrement at calls plays that role).
design_question: What extra structure (fuel or a well-founded measure) is genuinely needed for circular modular verification to compose?

tier_justification: The classical failure of the circular rule for termination, in the procedure-contract setting; Abadi and Lamport give the analogous failure of circular assume-guarantee for liveness.
plain_claim: The closed module `selfLoopMod = [(0, call 0 var)]` implements `zeroOutSpec` and satisfies the circular partial-correctness obligation (verified to return `0` assuming it returns `0`), yet is not totally correct.
depth_justification: `eval fuel selfLoopMod 0 0 = [outOfFuel]` for every fuel, by induction.
non_claims: Does not refute the circular rule for partial correctness (`ag-partial-correctness`).
Escape hatch: a well-founded measure decreasing across every call restores total correctness (`Toy.Link.Examples.positive_control_ag_total_with_wf_measure`, `ag-total-correctness-wf-measure`).
Non-termination appears as `outOfFuel` at every fuel; there is no separate infinite-trace semantics.
prior_art: Martín Abadi and Leslie Lamport, 'Conjoining specifications', ACM TOPLAS 17(3):507-535, 1995, doi:10.1145/203095.201069 (§2.2, 'Composing Open Systems', pp. 510-513: circular composition succeeds for the safety example 'c always equals 0' and fails for the liveness example 'c eventually equals 1'; an analogy in TLA over reactive systems, not a statement about procedures).
design_question: What extra structure (a well-founded measure) is genuinely needed for circular modular verification of total correctness?

tier_justification: Soundness of the total-correctness rule for mutually recursive procedures with a well-founded relation (Nipkow 2002, §§4-5), here with finite branching.
plain_claim: If `rel` is well-founded, `P` implements all satisfiable preconditions of `S`, and every body establishes its contract in `wpCallDec rel μ S` (every call strictly decreases the call measure `μ` and meets the callee precondition), then `P` is totally correct for `S` (a uniform finite fuel bound per argument).

hypotheses.name: WellFounded rel
hypotheses.purpose: forbids infinite descending call chains

hypotheses.name: SpecsImplemented P S
hypotheses.purpose: rules out `undefinedCall` at calls permitted by `S`

hypotheses.name: ModuleVerifiedTotal rel μ P S S
hypotheses.purpose: each body meets its postcondition while every call decreases `μ` and meets the callee precondition

depth_justification: Well-founded induction on `μ fn x` with an inner structural induction on bodies, fuel stabilization (`eval_stabilizes_of_no_outOfFuel`) and a maximum over finitely many branches.
nonvacuity_witness: `evenOddProg` with `WellFounded Nat.lt` and `μ _ x := x.toNat`. Applying the theorem yields `ProgramTotalCorrect evenOddProg evenOddSpec` (`Toy.Link.Examples.evenOddProg_total_correct`); the empty module with the unsatisfiable `falseSpec` is a degenerate instance (`Toy.Link.Examples.empty_module_ag_total`).
non_claims: The uniform fuel bound per argument depends on finite (binary) branching; with unbounded nondeterminism a uniform finite bound can fail even when every execution terminates, and total-correctness proofs need countable ordinals (Apt and Plotkin 1986).

Contracts are on a single integer argument and result; no state, frames, auxiliary variables or adaptation rules are modelled; integers are unbounded; every call (recursive or not) must decrease the measure, which depends only on the callee and its argument.
If `S` is too weak to establish the measure decrease for a later call, `wpCallDec` is unprovable even for terminating code (incompleteness of this particular rule is not studied).

One measure `(rel, μ)` must be shared by every function of the program, including across linked modules (`Toy.Link.link_ag_total_correctness_of_wf_call_measure` takes the same `rel` and `μ` for both modules). Modules verified separately with their own well-founded measures do not compose: `pingMod = [(0, call 1 var)]` and `pongMod = [(1, call 0 var)]` are each verified for total correctness over `Nat.lt` with measures `μ₁ fn _ = if fn = 0 then 1 else 0` and `μ₂ fn _ = if fn = 1 then 1 else 0`, their link implements the interface, and the linked program is not totally correct (`Toy.Link.Cex.independent_measures_do_not_compose`).
prior_art: Tobias Nipkow, 'Hoare logics for recursive procedures and unbounded nondeterminism', CSL 2002, LNCS 2471, pp. 103-119, Springer, 2002, doi:10.1007/3-540-45793-3_8 (§4: total correctness with well-founded relations; §5.2: CALL rule with a well-founded relation for mutually recursive procedures; mechanized in Isabelle/HOL).

K. R. Apt and G. D. Plotkin, 'Countable nondeterminism and random assignment', Journal of the ACM 33(4):724-767, 1986, doi:10.1145/6490.6494 (countable nondeterminism breaks continuity; total-correctness proofs need countable ordinals).
Norbert Schirmer, Simpl, Archive of Formal Proofs, 2008 (total-correctness Hoare logic with recursive procedures and unbounded nondeterminism, in Isabelle/HOL).
design_question: What extra structure (a well-founded measure) is genuinely needed for circular modular verification of total correctness?

tier_justification: The rule of recursive invocation for the caller's own functions combined with the consequence rule (refinement-calculus ordering) for imports.
plain_claim: If a caller module `M` is verified for its guarantee `G` assuming `G` for calls to its own functions and `S` for all other calls (`ModuleVerifiedPartial M (mixEnv M G S) G`), and a disjoint callee module `N` is partially correct for a spec `S'` that refines `S` at every name `M` does not define (weaker precondition, postcondition strengthened under the precondition), then every function of `M` is partially correct for `G` in `link M N`; `M` may be recursive.

hypotheses.name: Linkable M N
hypotheses.purpose: without disjointness, a call inside `N` can be captured by `M`'s definition of the same name (symbol interposition)

hypotheses.name: ModuleVerifiedPartial M (mixEnv M G S) G
hypotheses.purpose: `M`'s bodies satisfy `G`, assuming `G` for internal calls and `S` for external calls

hypotheses.name: ProgramPartialCorrect N S'
hypotheses.purpose: `N` satisfies `S'` on its own (and therefore implements every name with a satisfiable `S'` precondition)

hypotheses.name: ∀ g, ¬ M.Defines g → WeakensPre (S g) (S' g)
hypotheses.purpose: every external call argument allowed by the assumed precondition is allowed by the callee's precondition

hypotheses.name: ∀ g, ¬ M.Defines g → StrengthensPostUnderPre (S g) (S' g)
hypotheses.purpose: every result the callee may return (under the assumed precondition) satisfies the assumed postcondition

depth_justification: Induction on fuel; internal calls use the induction hypothesis at `G`, external calls use `eval_link_right_of_no_undefinedCall` and the refinement of `S` by `S'`; one-frame soundness `wpPartial_sound_evalExprWith`.
nonvacuity_witness: Recursive caller `recCaller = [(0, ifLe var (lit 0) (call 1 var) (call 0 (sub var (lit 1))))]` (reachable internal call to `0`, external call to `1`) with guarantee `v ≥ 10`, assuming `1` returns at least `10` on `x ≤ 0`, linked with `tenLib = [(1, lit 10)]` satisfying the strictly stronger spec `pre True, post v = 10`. Applying the theorem yields `FnPartialCorrect (link recCaller tenLib) 0 (recGuar 0)` (`Toy.Link.Examples.positive_control_spec_refinement_link`).
non_claims: The callee `N` must be partially correct for `S'` on its own: it may not call back into `M` (an unresolved call is `undefinedCall`, which `ProgramPartialCorrect` forbids). Mutually recursive caller/callee pairs need `link_ag_partial_correctness` with a shared interface.

The flat variant `Toy.Link.verified_flat_caller_links_with_refined_callee` (assumptions `S` for every call, refinement at every name) follows from this theorem but applies only to callers that make no verifiable call to their own functions: its hypotheses force `(S f).pre` to be unsatisfiable at every `f` that `M` defines (`Toy.Link.caller_spec_unsat_on_own_symbols`, `Toy.Link.Cex.flat_spec_refinement_inapplicable_to_recursive_caller`).
Partial correctness only: divergence is not observed; no termination or behavioural refinement is established.
Contracts are on a single integer argument and result; no state, frames, auxiliary variables or adaptation rules are modelled; integers are unbounded.
prior_art: C. A. R. Hoare, 'Procedures and parameters: An axiomatic approach', LNM 188, pp. 102-116, Springer, 1971, doi:10.1007/BFb0059696 (rule of recursive invocation; the page of the rule was not checked).
C. A. R. Hoare, 'An axiomatic basis for computer programming', Communications of the ACM 12(10):576-580, 1969, doi:10.1145/363235.363259 (rule of consequence).

Carroll Morgan, Programming from Specifications, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall International, 1994 (checked in the author's 1998 reissue): Law 1.2 'weaken precondition' and Law 5.1 'strengthen postcondition' (if pre[w\w0] ∧ post' ⇛ post then w:[pre, post] ⊑ w:[pre, post']), which is exactly the `WeakensPre` / `StrengthensPostUnderPre` ordering.

Barbara H. Liskov and Jeannette M. Wing, 'A behavioral notion of subtyping', ACM TOPLAS 16(6):1811-1841, 1994, doi:10.1145/197320.197383 (Fig. 4, p. 1823: precondition rule and an unconditional postcondition rule, a stricter precursor of the ordering used here).
design_question: What spec-refinement structure lets a verified caller, including one with internal recursive calls, be linked with any callee implementation satisfying a refining spec?

tier_justification: Direct instance showing that a callee spec better on the precondition side but not refining on the postcondition side does not protect the caller.
plain_claim: The caller `incCaller = [(0, call 1 (lit 0))]`, verified for `v = 10` assuming `1` satisfies `pre x ≥ 0, post v = 10`, linked with `incCallee = [(1, lit 11)]`, which satisfies the incomparable spec `pre True, post v ≥ 10` (the precondition side refines, the postcondition side does not, and the assumed spec does not refine it either), violates the caller's guarantee.
depth_justification: Concrete evaluation at fuel `2` by `decide`; spec facts by `simp`.
non_claims: The failure here is due to the postcondition side alone (`WeakensPre` holds at every external name). The precondition side is witnessed separately by `Toy.Link.Cex.cex_spec_refinement_without_weakensPre`.
Does not claim that every incomparable spec causes a failure: only a caller that relies on the part of `S` that `S'` does not guarantee is unprotected.
Partial correctness only; toy contracts on one integer argument and result.
prior_art: Carroll Morgan, Programming from Specifications, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall International, 1994 (Law 5.1 'strengthen postcondition').
Barbara H. Liskov and Jeannette M. Wing, ACM TOPLAS 16(6):1811-1841, 1994, doi:10.1145/197320.197383 (Fig. 4, p. 1823, postcondition rule).
design_question: Which spec relations between assumed and actual callee specs are needed for linking a verified caller?

tier_justification: A corollary of the assume-guarantee rule (`ag-partial-correctness`) applied to compiled modules: specification preservation in the sense of Leroy 2009, §2.1, property (4), at module granularity; compare certificate translation (Barthe et al. 2009). Semantic separate-compilation results (CompCertM, CompCertO, Patterson and Ahmed) are a contrast, not the source.
plain_claim: If `M₁` and `M₂` are verified against the interface `S`, `link M₁ M₂` implements `S`, and a per-module pass `compile` preserves verification against `S` (`PreservesVerifiedPartial`) and keeps every defined name (`PreservesDefines`), then the separately compiled linked program `link (compile M₁) (compile M₂)` is partially correct for `S`; no behavioural relation to the source is claimed.

hypotheses.name: ModuleVerifiedPartial M₁ S S
hypotheses.purpose: first module verified against `S` before compilation

hypotheses.name: ModuleVerifiedPartial M₂ S S
hypotheses.purpose: second module verified against `S` before compilation

hypotheses.name: SpecsImplemented (link M₁ M₂) S
hypotheses.purpose: every name with a satisfiable precondition exists in the source link

hypotheses.name: PreservesVerifiedPartial compile S
hypotheses.purpose: the pass maps `S`-verified modules to `S`-verified modules, looking at no other module. Only its instances at `M₁` and `M₂` are used; the universal pass property is stronger than needed.

hypotheses.name: PreservesDefines compile
hypotheses.purpose: the pass keeps the names that `SpecsImplemented` needs. Only its instances at `M₁` and `M₂` are used.

depth_justification: Definitional given `ag_partial_correctness`: it is `link_ag_partial_correctness` applied to `compile M₁` and `compile M₂`, with the two pass hypotheses producing its premises.
nonvacuity_witness: `sepMod1 = [(0, add (call 1 var) (lit 0))]` and `sepMod2 = [(1, add (lit 0) var)]`, verified against `sepSpec` (functions `0` and `1` accept every argument and return it; every other name has an unsatisfiable precondition), compiled by the non-identity constant folder `constFoldPass` (which rewrites `e + 0` and `0 + e` to `e`). The three helper definitions are `private` in the Lean source and are printed in REPORT.md.
non_claims: The theorem relates no behaviour of the compiled program to the source program. `PreservesVerifiedPartial compile S` mentions only `S`, so a pass satisfying both preservation hypotheses may replace every body by any code meeting `S`. Example: with interface `v ≥ 0`, the pass `zeroBodies` rewrites `1` to `0`, satisfies both hypotheses, but breaks `EntryRefines` with the source (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_verifiability_preservation_not_behavioural`). The guarantee is `S`-correctness of the compiled program, not semantic preservation; for behavioural refinement see `separate-compilation-behavioural-refinement`.
This result is `link_ag_partial_correctness` applied to the compiled modules; `compile` enters only through the two preservation hypotheses.
Partial correctness only: not total correctness, timing, or divergence behaviour.
Does not assume `Linkable M₁ M₂`: `moduleVerifiedPartial_link` only checks bodies reachable via `lookup (link M₁ M₂)`, although real linkers reject duplicate definitions.
A pass whose correctness depends on another module's implementation, not just on `S`, violates `PreservesVerifiedPartial` (`Toy.Link.Cex.inlPass_not_preservesVerified`).
prior_art: Xavier Leroy, 'Formal verification of a realistic compiler', Communications of the ACM 52(7):107-115, 2009, doi:10.1145/1538788.1538814 (§2.1, property (4): the compiler preserves the fact that the source satisfies a specification; stated for whole programs).

Gilles Barthe, Benjamin Grégoire, César Kunz, and Tamara Rezk, 'Certificate translation for optimizing compilers', ACM TOPLAS 31(5), 45 pp., 2009, doi:10.1145/1538917.1538919 (transforming proofs of source-program properties into certificates for the compiled program).
Youngju Song et al., 'CompCertM', PACMPL 4(POPL), Article 23, 2020, doi:10.1145/3371091 (§4.2, verification against specification modules; contrast: semantic refinement, not established here).
design_question: What does separate compilation preserve when passes are only required to preserve per-module verifiability against interface specs?

tier_justification: Separate compilation correctness from per-module contextual refinement, in the shape of Patterson and Ahmed's Corollary 4.3, here immediate from the precongruence of `CtxRefines`.
plain_claim: If a per-module pass is a contextual refinement on every module (`PassCtxRefines compile`, behaviour relation `CtxRefines`) and `M₁`, `M₂` are disjoint, then `link (compile M₁) (compile M₂)` contextually refines `link M₁ M₂`; in particular partial correctness of the source link transfers to the compiled link.

hypotheses.name: PassCtxRefines compile
hypotheses.purpose: explicit behaviour relation: each compiled module contextually refines its source (only the instances at `M₁` and `M₂` are used); used by both theorems; the named counterexample refutes the conclusion `CtxRefines (link M₁ M₂) (link (compile M₁) (compile M₂))` of the primary theorem `separate_compilation_ctxRefines_of_pass_ctxRefines`, not the corollary's conclusion `ProgramPartialCorrect (link (compile M₁) (compile M₂)) S` (its other conjuncts discharge every hypothesis of `separate_compilation_partial_correct_of_preserves_verified`, so its compiled link is partially correct for `zSpec`); the package does not exhibit a counterexample to the corollary without this premise

hypotheses.name: Linkable M₁ M₂
hypotheses.purpose: disjointness, as in the precongruence theorem; an overlapping module can shadow names the other relies on; used by both theorems; the named counterexample refutes the conclusion `CtxRefines (link M₁ M₂) (link (compile M₁) (compile M₂))` of the primary theorem, not the corollary's partial-correctness conclusion; the package does not exhibit a counterexample to the corollary without this premise

hypotheses.name: ProgramPartialCorrect (link M₁ M₂) S
hypotheses.purpose: third premise (`hSrc`) of the corollary `separate_compilation_preserves_partial_correctness_of_pass_ctxRefines` only: the property that is transferred to the compiled link; the corollary produces no correctness fact that the source link does not already have

nonvacuity_witness: The constant folder `constFoldPass` is a contextual refinement on every module (it does not change any outcome list), with the disjoint modules `sepMod1 = [(0, add (call 1 var) (lit 0))]` and `sepMod2 = [(1, add (lit 0) var)]` (`Toy.Link.Examples.nonvacuous_separate_compilation_ctxRefines`). For all three premises of the corollary: the same pass with the public copies `scMod1 = [(0, add (call 1 var) (lit 0))]`, `scMod2 = [(1, add (lit 0) var)]` and the interface `scSpec` (functions `0` and `1` return their argument), whose source link is partially correct; the corollary then gives partial correctness of the compiled link (`Toy.Link.Examples.nonvacuous_sep_comp_behavioural_corollary`).
non_claims: The behaviour relation is `CtxRefines`, which compares outcomes in lockstep call depth, includes `outOfFuel`, and forces equal domains; passes that introduce helpers never satisfy it (`Toy.Link.ctxRefines_sameDom`), and passes that add or remove calls or inline need not (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_ctxRefines_fixes_call_depth`), so such passes are not covered unless `CtxRefines` is proved for them.
Same-language, stateless, first-order modules only: unlike CompCertO Theorem 3.8 or Patterson and Ahmed's Corollary 4.3, there is no change of language, memory model, or calling convention.

Behavioural refinement preserves partial correctness for the same specs; verifiability preservation does not imply behavioural refinement (`Toy.Link.Cex.cex_verifiability_preservation_not_behavioural`).
prior_art: Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, 'The next 700 compiler correctness theorems (functional pearl)', PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§4.1, Theorem 4.1 (CCC), p. 85:8; §4.2, Corollary 4.3 'CCC Implies Correct Separate Compilation', p. 85:9).
Jérémie Koenig and Zhong Shao, 'CompCertO', PLDI '21, pp. 1095-1109, 2021, doi:10.1145/3453483.3454097 (§3.4, Theorem 3.8: compositional correctness of CompCertO).

Jeehoon Kang, Yoonseung Kim, Chung-Kil Hur, Derek Dreyer, and Viktor Vafeiadis, 'Lightweight verification of separate compilation', POPL '16, pp. 178-190, 2016, doi:10.1145/2837614.2837642 (separate compilation correctness for modules compiled by the same compiler).
design_question: What does separate compilation preserve when passes are required to be per-module behavioural refinements?

tier_justification: Folklore distinction between specification preservation and semantic preservation, made precise with a two-line pass.
plain_claim: The pass `zeroBodies` (replace every body by `lit 0`) preserves verification against the interface `zSpec` (`0` returns a non-negative value) and keeps every name, and all hypotheses of `separate-compilation-preserves-verifiability` hold for `const1Mod` and the empty module; yet the compiled program returns `0` where the source returns `1`, so it neither refines the source at entry `0` nor contextually, and `zeroBodies` is not a contextually refining pass.
depth_justification: Pass properties by a lookup lemma for `zeroBodies`; separation by `decide` at fuel `1`.
nonvacuity_witness: Source `const1Mod = [(0, lit 1)]` returns `1`; compiled `[(0, lit 0)]` returns `0`.
non_claims: Does not say verifiability-preserving passes are useless: the compiled program is still `S`-correct. It says that `S`-correctness is all they guarantee.
A pass may satisfy both properties (`Toy.Link.Examples.positive_control_constFold_verifiable_and_behavioural`).
prior_art: Xavier Leroy, CACM 52(7):107-115, 2009, doi:10.1145/1538788.1538814 (§2.1: semantic preservation versus property (4), preservation of specifications).
design_question: What does separate compilation preserve when passes are only required to preserve per-module verifiability?

tier_justification: Folklore hazard (a per-module optimization justified by another module's body rather than its interface) made into a minimal mechanized witness; no mechanized witness of this kind was found.
plain_claim: Rewriting the caller `inlCaller = [(0, call 1 var)]` to `inlCallerOpt = [(0, (call 1 var + call 1 var) - 2)]` is a contextual equivalence in the whole program with `inlCallee1 = [(1, lit 2)]`, but it is not a per-module contextual refinement and not verifiable against the shared interface `inlSpec`; replacing `inlCallee1` by `inlCallee2 = [(1, lit 1)]`, which also satisfies `inlSpec` and keeps the original program correct, makes the rewritten program return `0`, violating `inlSpec` and refinement.
depth_justification: Contextual equivalence under `inlCallee1` by fuel induction; separations by `decide` at fuel `2`.
non_claims: The transformation is not inlining; it is an algebraic rewrite valid only for the specific callee body, and it keeps both calls.

Does not invalidate link-time optimization when all participating bodies are fixed together; it shows that a per-module rewrite justified by another module's body is neither a per-module contextual refinement nor verification-preserving (`Toy.Link.Cex.inlPass_not_preservesVerified`), so neither separate-compilation theorem covers it.
The positive control covers two concrete spec-compliant callees; the statement for every spec-compliant callee is `link_ag_partial_correctness`.
prior_art: Jeehoon Kang, Yoonseung Kim, Chung-Kil Hur, Derek Dreyer, and Viktor Vafeiadis, 'Lightweight verification of separate compilation', POPL '16, pp. 178-190, 2016, doi:10.1145/2837614.2837642 (§5.3: intra-module inlining stays valid after linking because the inlined definitions remain in the linked environment; contrast with a rewrite that depends on another module).
Daniel Patterson and Amal Ahmed, PACMPL 3(ICFP), Article 85, 2019, doi:10.1145/3341689 (§3: compiler correctness theorems differ in what code a compiled module may be linked with).
design_question: Which per-module transformations are compatible with interface-only (spec-based) separate compilation?
